description: General architecture, maintainability, testing, security and delivery. Review applicability before adoption.

rules.title: Separate coherent responsibilities
rules.guidance: SHOULD separate business rules, presentation and infrastructure. Keep methods focused on a coherent responsibility; do not enforce arbitrary method-length limits.

rules.title: Invert infrastructure dependencies
rules.guidance: SHOULD keep business logic independent of concrete IO implementations. Supply infrastructure through explicit interfaces and injection at composition boundaries; do not add interfaces without a useful boundary.

rules.title: Keep knowledge authoritative
rules.guidance: SHOULD reuse authoritative business rules rather than copy them. Similar syntax alone does not justify coupling unrelated concepts through an abstraction.
rules.rationale: Avoid inconsistent rules and premature abstraction.

rules.title: Solve the current problem
rules.guidance: SHOULD use the simplest design meeting approved requirements. Avoid speculative features, unnecessary layers and unmeasured microservice splits.

rules.title: Make code understandable
rules.guidance: SHOULD use domain-relevant names and straightforward control flow. Explain non-obvious decisions in comments; remove misleading or obsolete comments.

rules.title: Keep usage documentation current
rules.guidance: MUST update relevant setup, API, configuration and operational documentation when behavior changes. Explain compatibility impacts and migrations where applicable.

rules.title: Keep changes reviewable
rules.guidance: SHOULD keep changes focused on the requested outcome. Separate unrelated refactoring or formatting and explain unavoidable scope expansion.

rules.title: Follow adopted repository conventions
rules.guidance: MUST use the repository's configured style and checks. Do not introduce conflicting conventions or suppress diagnostics without explaining the reason.

rules.title: Test meaningful behavior
rules.guidance: MUST add tests for changed behavior, failures and important boundaries. Choose unit, integration or end-to-end tests according to risk; assert outcomes rather than implementation trivia.

rules.title: Keep tests independent
rules.guidance: MUST make tests independent of execution order and leftover state. Control time, randomness and external services where feasible, while retaining representative integration tests.

rules.title: Use coverage to find gaps
rules.guidance: MUST meet explicitly adopted coverage targets and review untested critical paths. Do not invent a universal percentage or equate coverage with correctness.

rules.title: Report checks honestly
rules.guidance: MUST run applicable repository checks before reporting completion. State executed checks, failures and checks that could not run; never infer a pass from an unexecuted check.

rules.title: Separate deployment configuration
rules.guidance: MUST read deployment-specific values through the approved configuration mechanism. Validate required values at startup; keep stable business rules in code or governed domain configuration.

rules.title: Protect credentials
rules.guidance: MUST obtain credentials from approved secret mechanisms. Do not commit, hardcode or expose secrets in generated artifacts; use scoped credentials and the organization's rotation process.

rules.title: Log useful context safely
rules.guidance: MUST record relevant operational and security events with correlation context. Redact credentials and sensitive data; avoid logging complete request bodies by default.

rules.title: Make builds reproducible
rules.guidance: MUST declare dependencies and supported runtime versions. Use the ecosystem's lock or constraint mechanism where appropriate; avoid undeclared machine-global dependencies.

rules.title: Review dependency risk
rules.guidance: SHOULD prefer maintained dependencies and review vulnerabilities, provenance and applicable licenses before adoption. Do not silently add a dependency when existing capabilities suffice.

rules.title: Make failures explicit
rules.guidance: MUST distinguish expected errors from faults. Recover only when recovery is safe; do not swallow failures or expose internal exception details to users.

rules.title: Keep environments representative
rules.guidance: SHOULD keep test and deployment dependencies and configuration behavior sufficiently aligned to detect integration failures. Document unavoidable differences.

criteria.rubric: Pass only if the generated guidance separates responsibilities without arbitrary size limits. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
